html:
The Wampanoag, in their own language Wôpanâak, "People of the First Light", are an Algonquian people of southeastern Massachusetts, Cape Cod, Martha's Vineyard, Nantucket and eastern Rhode Island. They lived in villages led by sachems, growing maize, beans and squash and fishing along the coast. Their neighbours were the Narragansett to the west and the closely related Nauset of outer Cape Cod.

  • An epidemic brought by European traders killed a large part of them between 1616 and 1619.
  • In 1621 the sachem Massasoit made an alliance with the English of Plymouth Colony, helped by Tisquantum (Squanto), who spoke English after being kidnapped to Europe. The harvest feast that autumn is remembered as the First Thanksgiving.
  • His son Metacom, called King Philip by the English, led King Philip's War of 1675 to 1676 against the spreading colonies. It ended in defeat, and many Wampanoag were killed or sold into slavery in the Caribbean.

Communities survived at Mashpee and Aquinnah. Since the 1990s a reclamation project has brought back the language, unspoken for over a century, using documents written in it in colonial times.
